findings.summary: ARIMA is a statistical model for time series that generalizes ARMA to handle non-stationary data and seasonal patterns. It combines three components: autoregressive (AR) terms that regress the series on its own lags, moving average (MA) terms that model error as a linear combination of past errors, and differencing (I) that removes trends or seasonal cycles to achieve stationarity. The model is specified by orders (p,d,q) where p is AR order, d is differencing depth, and q is MA order. Seasonal extensions add seasonal AR, differencing, and MA terms with a period length m. Model order selection uses information criteria like AIC, AICc, or BIC, balancing fit against parameter count. Forecasts are produced by cascading a differencing step with a stationary ARMA sub-model.

mechanisms.title: Differencing for stationarity
mechanisms.explanation: The integrated (I) component removes non-stationary trends by subtracting prior observations. First-order differencing computes y_t' = y_t - y_{t-1}; second-order differencing applies differencing twice. Seasonal differencing subtracts the observation m periods ago (y_t - y_{t-m}) to eliminate periodic variation. This transforms the series so that standard ARMA models can be applied.

mechanisms.title: AR and MA sub-model specification
mechanisms.explanation: After differencing, the remaining stationary series is modeled as an ARMA(p,q) process. The autoregressive part models the variable as a linear regression on its own prior values. The moving average part models the error term as a linear combination of recent error shocks. Parameters are estimated by fitting the cascaded model, and forecasts are generated by projecting forward from this stationary core.
